::: {.facts .k-strep}
[At a glance]{.facts-label}

Group
: *Streptococcus anginosus* group, with *S. anginosus* and *S. constellatus*

Gram stain
: Gram-positive cocci in chains

Habitat
: Normal flora of the mouth, upper airway, gut and genitourinary tract

Known for
: Abscesses, especially in the brain and liver

Key toxin
: Intermedilysin, which targets human cells through CD59
:::

## The organism

Older papers call this group the "*Streptococcus milleri* group". Lancefield grouping is unreliable here: isolates can carry group A, C, F or G antigens, or none. On culture, the group is often described as smelling of caramel. Identification now relies on MALDI-TOF or sequencing, because biochemical tests struggle to separate the three species.

## Why it matters clinically

All three species can cause invasive infection, but *S. intermedius* is the one most often linked to brain and liver abscesses. Brain abscesses often have a dental or sinus source.

## Intermedilysin

Intermedilysin is a cholesterol-dependent cytolysin, a pore-forming toxin. Most toxins in this family bind cholesterol on any cell, but intermedilysin first binds human CD59, so it damages human cells far more readily than those of other animals.
